_notes: Augustinian career, third pool: the friends lapsing and splitting, the third restlessness, the pastor and the bishop, the college's presidency, the old friar dying, the house of four, the mountain in the parish, the province merging. E3 §12, §14.

events.title: The Letters Stopped
events.body: The weekly letter has not come for two months and you have not written either, since a house and a parish and a school will do that, and the formation director's rule was a letter a week and the rule has lapsed, which is how the three lapse, {@old_friar} says: not by a quarrel but by a Tuesday, and then another. There is paper on the desk.

choices.label: Write tonight, and say the two months
choices.outcome: He writes back the next day, which he had not done in two months, and says he had been waiting to be written to, since he had thought it was his turn, and it was, and the letters are weekly again and neither of you keeps count after that, since the counting was the problem.

choices.label: Telephone; the paper is for the life and this is the life
choices.outcome: He answers and is glad and is surprised, since the telephone was for emergencies, and you say it is one, and he laughs, and it is an hour, and the letters are the letters again, and the telephone is used, after that, for the Tuesdays.

choices.label: Let it lie; friendships in the order come and go
choices.outcome: It goes. He is a friar four hours away for the rest of your life and you see him at chapters and are glad and are not friends, and the old friar says that was one of the three, and that men do not get four, and you learn it late.

events.title: The Two Houses
events.body: {@confrere} was moved and the friendship was moved with him, and the letters carry it, mostly, and this year they carry something else: his house and yours are on opposite sides of a thing the province is dividing over, and he has written a page on his house's side, and it is a good page, and the house you live in has read it, since houses read letters left on tables.

choices.label: Write back that you are with him, and let the house see it
choices.outcome: The house sees it. It is a cold month at the table and then it is not, since the house had known you had one of your three on the other side, and had wanted to see what you would do, and you did, and the old friar says you chose the man over the house, and that the founder would have.

choices.label: Write back that you are with your house, and say why
choices.outcome: He writes back that he had expected it and is glad you said why, and the friendship holds, thinner, for a year, and then the province decides the thing and it does not matter, and the two of you never mention the page again, which is a kind of scar.

choices.label: Write back about something else entirely
choices.outcome: He understands, since he is a friar, and writes back about something else too, and the thing the province is dividing over is decided without either of you having said, and the friendship has a room in it that neither enters, and it holds, and the room stays.

events.title: The Third Time
events.body: It is the third time, and it is the one the founder wrote about, and it has come in a good year, as they do, and it is larger than the two before it and it has, this time, a door in it, which the others did not: a sense that there is a place past it that is not the same place, and {@old_friar}, who has had four, says the third is the one that either makes a friar or unmakes him, and that he cannot tell which from the outside.

choices.label: Go through it: the chapel, every night, for as long as it takes
choices.outcome: It takes a year. On the far side of it is the thing the founder called rest, or the beginning of it, and you are a different man at the table, and the house sees it and does not have a word for it, and the old friar does: he says you have been made, and that he is glad he lived to see it.

choices.label: Go through it with the friend beside you
choices.outcome: He comes and stays a week, which his prior allows, and the two of you say the Office at every hour for the week, and it is not enough and it is the beginning, and the rest of it is yours, and takes the year, and he is in every letter of it, and it is what the three are for.

choices.label: Go out the door instead: ask the provincial for a year away
choices.outcome: He gives it, since he has read the founder too. The year is a year in the world and it is good and it is not the place past the restlessness, and you come back, or do not, and if you come back the third time is waiting where you left it, and you go through it then, older.

events.title: The Pastor's Parish
events.body: Pastor, of the parish the house runs, and the parish is the house's and the bishop's and yours, which is three owners for one thing, and the first month has produced a conflict between the first two: the bishop's office wants the parish to merge its Masses with the diocesan parish next door, and the house wants the eleven o'clock kept, since the house sings it, and the pastor is the one who answers the bishop.

choices.label: Do as the bishop's office asks, and tell the house why
choices.outcome: The house is cold for a season and then the merged Mass is full, which the eleven o'clock was not, and the house sings it anyway, since it is a Mass, and the bishop's office says the friars were reasonable, which it had not said in a decade, and the house says the pastor was the bishop's man, for a year, and then does not.

choices.label: Keep the eleven o'clock, and write to the bishop's office that the house sings it
choices.outcome: The office is not pleased and lets it stand, since it is a small thing, and the eleven o'clock is thin and beautiful and the house is grateful, and the office remembers, and the next thing it asks is not small, and the pastor who kept the eleven o'clock is the one it asks.

choices.label: Merge the Masses, and move the house's sung Mass to Sunday evening
choices.outcome: Both are startled. The Sunday evening Mass is the parish's largest in three years, since the students come, and the house sings it, and the bishop's office says the friars were clever, which is not praise and is not not, and the parish has a Mass that is the house's and the bishop's and yours.

events.title: The Curate Is a Friar
events.body: The province has sent you a curate, a friar of two years, and he is a good priest and a bad Augustinian: he eats in the office, says the Office alone, and has, in a month, become the parish's favourite and the house's stranger, and {@prior} has said, at chapter, that it is the pastor's to fix, since it is the parish that has him, and the house that has lost him.

choices.label: Bring him to the table: eat with him in the office until he eats in the refectory
choices.outcome: It takes a season. You eat in the office with him, which the house finds odd, and then he eats in the refectory with you, which the house finds right, and by Easter he is a friar and a curate both, and says at his own first priory that a pastor sat in his office for a season, and that it was the thing.

choices.label: Tell him, once, plainly, what the house needs
choices.outcome: He hears it and is hurt and does it, since he is obedient, and is at the table and is not at it, and the house says he is present and the parish says he is less, and it is a year before he is either, and he does not say it was the telling, and it was.

choices.label: Leave him; the parish is glad of him and the house will manage
choices.outcome: The house manages, and the parish is glad, and he is the last curate of that kind the province sends you, since the prior writes to the provincial, and the next curate is a friar and a worse priest, and the parish notices, and so do you.

events.title: The Chapter Divides
events.body: The provincial chapter, and the thing it is dividing over is the thing every chapter of the province has divided over for twenty years: the schools or the parishes, since the province cannot staff both and has said so at every chapter and has done nothing at any of them. The moderator has asked whether anyone has a thing to say that has not been said, and the aula is quiet, and you have one.

choices.label: Say it: the province should choose, and here is how
choices.outcome: It is ten minutes and it is the thing, and the aula is silent after it and then is not, and the chapter does not choose, since chapters do not, but the next one does, and the men who were there say it was the speech, and the men who were not say it was the numbers, and it was both.

choices.label: Ask the chapter a question instead: what the province will look like in fifteen years
choices.outcome: Nobody can answer it and the moderator sends it to a commission, which answers it, and the answer is a number, and the number chooses, four years later, and the chapter says the commission did it, and the commission says it was the question, and you sat down after asking it.

choices.label: Say nothing; the thing will be said by someone with more years
choices.outcome: It is said, by someone with more years, badly, and the chapter divides as it always has, and you drive home with {@confrere} and say the thing to him in the car, and he says you should have said it in the aula, and you know it, and say it at the next chapter, four years on.

events.title: The Bishop's Office Writes
events.body: The bishop's office has written to the provincial for you by name, for a diocesan post: the diocesan director of something, three years, an office in the chancery and a car, and the provincial has sent the letter to the prior and the prior has given it to you at breakfast with the words that it is a compliment and a problem, since a friar in the chancery is a friar the house does not have.

choices.label: Take it; the province needs the bishop
choices.outcome: Three years in a chancery. The bishop is glad of you and says so, and the province is, since the bishop is, and the house is not, since it is seven, and the three years are five, and you come back to the house a chancery man, which the house forgives in a year, and the bishop's office remembers for twenty.

choices.label: Decline; a friar is for a house
choices.outcome: The provincial declines it for you, courteously, and the bishop's office is courteous back and asks the next order, and the Dominicans send a man, and the house is eight and glad, and the province's standing with the bishop is what it was, which was not much.

choices.label: Offer two days a week, and the house the rest
choices.outcome: The bishop's office takes it, since two days of a friar is more than it had, and it is two days for four years and the house has you the other five, and the bishop says at a dinner that the friars are the only order that shares, which was not what the house had meant and was true.

events.title: The College Wants a President
events.body: The college's president is retiring and the trustees have said they would like one more friar, if the province has one, and the province has one, the provincial has written to say, and it is you, and the office is a house on the campus and a budget of a size the province has never seen and a board of laymen who will be kind and will not be obedient, and the prior has said the house will miss you and that it is the college that is the order's future, or was.

choices.label: Take it
choices.outcome: Six years. The college is a college and you are its president, which is a job and not a vocation, and it is done well, and the board is kind and is not obedient, and the friars' house on campus is the best community you live in, since it is the men who chose to teach, and the province says you kept the college the order's for six more years, and it was.

choices.label: Decline; the college will be lay and should have a lay president now
choices.outcome: The provincial is quiet and then says he had hoped for that answer and had not expected it, and the college takes a layman, and is a lay college with the order's name, and you are in a house, and the province says you gave the college away, and the board says you gave it a future, and both are true.

choices.label: Take it for two years, to find the layman
choices.outcome: The board agrees, since two years of a friar who is looking is what it wanted. You find the layman and he is good and the college is his in two years, and the province says you did what the college needed and not what the province wanted, and the board gives you a chair with your name on it, which the Rule has views on.

events.title: The Old Friar Is Dying
events.body: {@old_friar} is dying, in the house, since the house has said he will die in the house and not in the infirmary, and the house has taken the watches, and it is the one of your three who was old when you were a pre-novice, and he has asked for you for the last watch, since, he says, you were the one who asked about the boiler, or the one who sat with him, or the one he chose, and it comes to the same.

choices.label: Say the Office with him until he cannot, and then for him
choices.outcome: He says it with you for two nights and then cannot, and you say it, and he dies during Lauds, at the psalm he liked, and the house comes in and finishes it, and the prior says at the funeral that he died in the Office, which is what he wanted, and you were the voice.

choices.label: Let him talk, since he has fifty years to tell
choices.outcome: He tells them, for two nights, and it is the province from the inside and the house from the beginning, and you write it down afterward, since nobody else has it, and it is in the archive, and the novice directors read it, and he is in it, alive.

choices.label: Sit with him in silence, since he kept it
choices.outcome: Two nights of it. He holds your hand at the end, which he had not done in forty years, and says one thing, which is the founder's word for rest, and dies, and you have the word, and use it, once, at your own end, to whoever is there.

events.title: The House Is Four
events.body: The house is four. It was eight when you came and the province has taken the others one by one, to the college and the mission and the grave, and four is the number below which the constitutions say a house is not a house, and the provincial has written to ask whether the house should close or be given, for a time, to the diocese's priests as a residence, and the four have met at the table, and it is your table.

choices.label: Close it, and go where the province sends
choices.outcome: The house closes. The four go to four houses and are, each of them, the old man of a new table, and the parish is the diocese's and misses the friars, and says so at the last Mass, and you preach it, and it is four minutes, and the founder's word is in it.

choices.label: Take the diocesan priests as residents, and be a house of four among six
choices.outcome: The two diocesan priests are good men and are not friars and do not eat at the table, at first, and then do, since the table is the table, and by the second year the house is six at supper and the constitutions say nothing about who the six are, and the provincial says it was Augustinian, and the bishop says it was hospitable, and both are right.

choices.label: Ask the province for one more friar, and promise a novice from the parish
choices.outcome: The province sends one, since you promised, and the novice comes from the parish, since you had been looking, and the house is five and then six, and is a house, and the provincial says you were the only prior who answered his letter with a plan, and it was a small plan, and it worked.

events.title: The Mountain in the Parish
events.body: The mission is behind you and it is in you: the language, which the parish has no one to speak to, the people, whom the parish has not met, and the thing the mountain does to a man, which is to make the parish's troubles small, and the parish has noticed that its troubles are small to you, and does not like it, and {@prior} has said so, kindly, at recreation.

choices.label: Tell the parish about the mountain, Sunday by Sunday
choices.outcome: It takes a year of homilies and the parish is, by the end of it, a parish that knows a mountain, and sends money to it, and a young couple goes for a summer, and the troubles are smaller to the parish too, which was the point, and the prior says the mountain came to the parish, and it did.

choices.label: Keep the mountain inside, and make the parish's troubles yours
choices.outcome: It takes a year and it works. The troubles are the size the parish thinks they are and you are the pastor the parish wanted, and the mountain is a thing you have at night, and in the letters to the friar who is still up there, and it is enough, and it is a cost.

choices.label: Ask to go back
choices.outcome: The provincial says no, since the province needs you here, and it is obedience and it is right, and the mountain is in the letters, and the parish is the parish, and in ten years the provincial is another man and says yes, and you go, old, and it is the same mountain.

events.title: The Hospital at Two
events.body: The parish's hospital has telephoned at two in the morning, as they do, for a priest, and it is your night, and the friar in the next cell has been awake, since he is, and has said through the door that he will go, since he cannot sleep and you can, and it is the third night this month he has said it, and he is not a man who cannot sleep.

choices.label: Go yourself, and knock on his door in the morning
choices.outcome: The hospital is the hospital. In the morning he is at the table and you sit by him and say nothing until he says the thing, which is that he has not slept in a month and does not know why, and you know why, since you have had it, and you tell him, and it is the third time for him and he had not known.

choices.label: Let him go; he asked
choices.outcome: He goes, and it is a good thing he did, since he is a good priest at two in the morning, and it is a month before you understand that he was going to the hospital because the cell was worse, and it is the prior who understands it first, and you had been asleep.

choices.label: Go together
choices.outcome: It is a strange thing, two friars at a bedside, and the family does not mind, and the drive back is the conversation he needed, since it is dark and the car is small, and he says the thing, and you say the founder's word, and he has not heard it since the novitiate, and it holds him for a while.

events.title: The Man Who Reads the Founder
events.body: The order's institute has asked the province for a friar to spend a year on the founder's sermons, editing, since the edition is fifty years old and wrong, and the provincial has written to say he thought of you, since the thesis was on the sermons, or since you preach from them, or since he had to think of someone, and the year is in a city with a library and no parish and a house of scholars, which the province does not have.

choices.label: Go, and edit
choices.outcome: The year is a year in a library and it is the strangest year of your life, since nobody needs you at two in the morning, and the edition is better for it, and the order's institute asks for a second year, and the province says no, and you come back, and preach from the sermons you edited, and they are better.

choices.label: Decline; the sermons were preached to a parish and you are in one
choices.outcome: The provincial says it was the Augustinian answer and sends someone else, who does it well, and the edition comes out and you preach from it, and it is better, and you had not done it, and the parish had you, and it is the trade.

choices.label: Offer the summers, for three years
choices.outcome: The institute takes it. Three summers in the library and nine months a year in the parish, and the edition is slower and is yours in part, and the parish has a pastor who disappears in July and comes back with sermons, which it says is odd and does not mind.

events.title: The Provinces May Merge
events.body: The province is to merge with the province next door, or may, since the numbers say it must and the chapters of both have said, for a decade, that it need not, and this year the order's general has written to say that it will, and has asked each province for a friar to sit on the commission that will do it, and the provincial has named you, and the house has said, at supper, that it is the end of the province, and it is.

choices.label: Serve on the commission, and do it well
choices.outcome: Two years of meetings. The merger is done well, which is the most a merger can be, and the new province is a province and not two, in ten years, and the old men of both say it was a loss, and the young men of both say it was a beginning, and you were in the room where it was decided which, and it was both.

choices.label: Serve, and argue for the province at every meeting
choices.outcome: The commission hears the argument and the merger happens anyway, since the numbers do not argue, and the old men of the province say you fought for it, and the new province remembers that you did, and it is a long time before it trusts you with anything, and then it does.

choices.label: Ask the provincial to name someone else
choices.outcome: He names someone else, who does it adequately, and the merger is done adequately, and the house says you did not want to be the man who ended the province, which was true, and the province is ended by someone else, and it is the same ending.

events.title: The Parish's Bad Year
events.body: The parish has had a bad year: three deaths in one family, a fire in the school, and a pastor who was moved in the middle of it, and the house has said the parish needs a friar who will sit with it, and has said it looking at you, since sitting is a thing the house thinks you do, and the family of the three deaths has asked for a Mass, and would like the homily to say something, and does not know what.

choices.label: Sit with them first, for a week, and then say what they said
choices.outcome: The homily is their words and they know it, and the parish, which came to see whether the friars could do this, sees that they can, and the family is at the priory every Sunday after, and the mother says, a year on, that it was the week and not the Mass, and it was both.

choices.label: Say the founder's thing about grief, from the Confessions, on his mother
choices.outcome: It is beautiful and the family hears it, some of them, and the parish hears it, more of them, and the house says it was the order at its best, and the mother says she would have liked less of the founder and more of her sons, and she was right, and it was still beautiful.

choices.label: Say three sentences, and let the Mass carry it
choices.outcome: The Mass carries it. The family is grateful and the parish is, and the house says the homily was short, and the mother says it was the right length, and you had not known which it was until she said.

events.title: The Young Friar's Third Time
events.body: A friar of the house, six years ordained, has come to your cell, which young friars do not do, and said that it has come a third time and that he does not know whether it is the founder's thing or the other thing, and has asked you since you are the one, he says, who went through it, and it shows, and he would like to know what it was like on the far side.

choices.label: Tell him what it was like, and that it takes a year
choices.outcome: He listens for an hour and goes through it, in a year, and is a different man at the table, and the house sees it, and he says at his jubilee that a friar told him it took a year and that the year was bearable because it had a number on it, and you had not known that was the thing you gave him.

choices.label: Say nothing, and go down to the chapel with him every night for a season
choices.outcome: The season is a winter and you are both in the chapel and neither says the thing, and it is the thing, and by Easter he is through it, or beginning to be, and says the chapel was the answer and that you had not said a word, and you had not needed to.

choices.label: Ask him who his three are, and whether they know
choices.outcome: He says two, and that they do not, and you say to telephone them tonight, and he does, and it is the friends who carry it, as the order says, and he says you sent him to them, and you say the order did, and it did.

events.title: The Boy at the Pantry
events.body: There is a boy at the parish's pantry on Tuesdays who has been there for two years, since he was fifteen, and who has begun to come to the friars' Vespers, and to sit at the back, and to leave before anyone can speak to him, and the woman who runs the pantry has said that he is going to ask, and that he does not know it yet, and that you should be the one he asks, since you were a pantry boy once, or a playground one.

choices.label: Wait at the back of the chapel after Vespers, until he stays
choices.outcome: It is three weeks. He stays. He asks, badly, and you answer, badly, since it is the first time for both, and he is a pre-novice in four years and a friar in ten, and the woman at the pantry says she knew, and she did.

choices.label: Ask him, at the pantry, on a Tuesday
choices.outcome: He is startled and says no, and comes to Vespers anyway, and asks two years later, on his own, and is a friar, and says the Tuesday was too early, and that it was also the day he knew, and the woman says both are true, and she would.

choices.label: Tell the vocation director, and let the office do it
choices.outcome: The office does it, well, and he is a pre-novice in three years, and says at profession that a friar from the province drove out to see him, and does not say that a friar at the back of the chapel did not, and you are at the profession, in the back, and it is enough, nearly.

events.title: The Diocesan Priest at the Door
events.body: A priest of the diocese, fifteen years ordained, a pastor, has come to the priory on a Tuesday and asked to see a friar, any friar, and has told you, in the parlour, that he is lonely in a way the diocese does not have a word for and the order does, and that he would like to know whether a man of forty-five can enter, and the constitutions say he can, and the province will say what the province says.

choices.label: Tell him the truth: the order is lonely too, differently
choices.outcome: He is quiet and says he had thought so and had wanted to hear it from a friar, and does not enter, and comes to supper once a month for twenty years, which the house allows, and is the diocesan priest the house is fondest of, and says the once a month was the thing, and it was.

choices.label: Tell him the order welcomes, and send him to the vocation director
choices.outcome: The vocation director sees him and the province takes him, since it takes men, and he is a novice at forty-six among men of twenty-four, and it is hard and he stays, and is a friar the province is glad of, and the bishop, who lost a pastor, is not glad, and says so.

choices.label: Ask him to supper, and say nothing about entering
choices.outcome: He comes to supper. The house does what it does, and he sees it, and asks, or does not, and either way he has seen a table, and the diocese has a pastor who knows what one looks like, and he builds one, in his rectory, with two other priests, and it lasts, and he says it was a Tuesday supper.

events.title: The Prior's Last Chapter
events.body: The last house chapter of the term, and the house has asked, as the constitutions allow, whether you would accept a second term if elected, and the house is looking at you, and {@old_friar} has said, going in, that a prior who says yes is a prior who has not finished and a prior who says no is one who has, and that he does not know which you are, and you are not sure either.

choices.label: Say yes
choices.outcome: The house elects you, or does not, and either way it heard a man say he had not finished, and if it elects you the second term is the one where the thing is finished, and the old friar says at its end that you were right, and if it does not, it says it would have, and you are in the ranks, and are glad, mostly.

choices.label: Say no, and why: the house should have another voice
choices.outcome: The house is quiet and then is grateful, since it is the truth, and elects another man, who is a good prior, and the ranks are the ranks, and the old friar says you finished, and that finishing is the rarer thing, and the new prior asks your advice in the second year and you give it briefly.

choices.label: Say the house should decide without your answer
choices.outcome: The house says that is not an answer and elects you anyway, or does not, and the old friar says a man who will not say is a man who wants both, and it was true, and the house knew it, and forgave it, since it was a good term.
